opex.text: Liquidity refers to the Company’s ability to generate sufficient cash to fund current loan demand, meet deposit withdrawals, pay operating expenses, and meet other obligations. Liquidity is monitored by the Company’s Asset Liability Committee. Other sources of liquidity include, but are not limited to, purchases of federal funds, advances from the FHLB, adjustments of interest rates to attract deposits, brokered deposits, and borrowing at the Federal Reserve discount window. Additionally, the Company could sell all of its AFS securities and the loss would not cause a change in the capital adequacy classification. Management believes its sources of liquidity are adequate to meet cash flow obligations for the foreseeable future.

prov.text: For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, the provision for credit losses and off-balance sheet commitments was $1.8 million, an increase of $322 thousand from $1.5 million in 2025. For more discussion see Results of Operations, three months. The provision for credit losses is determined based on management’s calculation of the adequacy of the allowance for credit losses, which includes provisions for classified loans as well as for the remainder of the portfolio based on historical data, including past charge-offs and current economic trends.

nonint.text: Noninterest expense increased $609 thousand, or 9%, from the third quarter 2025. Salary and employee benefit costs increased $468 thousand, or 11%, compared to the prior year quarter with an increase in base compensation levels as well as the number of full time equivalent employees increased from 181 in 2025 to 189 in 2026 as vacant positions were filled. Software expense increased $81 thousand, or 16%, and debit card expense increased $34 thousand, or 16%. Professional and director fees decreased $98 thousand, or 20%. The Company’s third quarter efficiency ratio decreased to 52.6% compared to 55.6% in the prior year.

nonop.text: Noninterest expense increased $609 thousand, or 9%, from the third quarter 2025. Salary and employee benefit costs increased $468 thousand, or 11%, compared to the prior year quarter with an increase in base compensation levels as well as the number of full time equivalent employees increased from 181 in 2025 to 189 in 2026 as vacant positions were filled. Software expense increased $81 thousand, or 16%, and debit card expense increased $34 thousand, or 16%. Professional and director fees decreased $98 thousand, or 20%. The Company’s third quarter efficiency ratio decreased to 52.6% compared to 55.6% in the prior year.

tax.text: The provision for income taxes was $3.5 million (effective rate of 19.8%) for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $2.8 million (effective rate of 19.6%) for the same period ended 2025.

net.text: For the quarters ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, the Company recorded net income of $5.0 million and $4.2 million and $1.90 and $1.57 per share, respectively. The $836 thousand increase in net income for the period was primarily the result of an increase of $1.7 million in net interest income and a $237 thousand increase in noninterest income. The noninterest expense increase of $609 thousand and an increase in the provision for credit losses and off-balance sheet commitments of $258 thousand partially offset the revenue increases. The federal income tax provision increased $214 thousand. Pre-provision net revenue ("PPNR"), (a non-GAAP measure), totaled $7 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, an increase of $1.3 million, or 23%, from the prior year's third quarter.

capex.text: The Company does not have any off-balance sheet arrangements (as such term is defined in applicable Securities and Exchange Commission (the “Commission”) rules) that are reasonably likely to have a current or future material effect on our financial condition, results of operations, liquidity, capital expenditures, or capital resources.

Noninterest income.text: Noninterest income increased $237 thousand, or 13%, compared to the third quarter of 2025. The increase was primarily the result of a $64 thousand increase in gain on sale of loans, a $55 thousand increase in debit card interchange fees, a $41 thousand increase in service charges on deposit accounts, and a $39 thousand increase in earnings on bank owned life insurance.

intro.text: CSB Bancorp, Inc. (“CSB”), is a registered financial holding company under the Bank Holding Company Act of 1956, as amended, and was incorporated under the laws of the State of Ohio in 1991. The Commercial and Savings Bank of Millersburg, Ohio (the “Bank”), an Ohio bank chartered in 1879, is a wholly owned subsidiary of CSB. The Bank is a member of the Federal Reserve System, and its deposits are insured up to the maximum amount provided by law by the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (“FDIC”). The primary regulators of the Bank are the Federal Reserve Board and the Ohio Division of Financial Institutions. CSB Investment Services, LLC, an Ohio limited liability company (“CSB Investment”), is a wholly owned subsidiary of CSB that is licensed to engage in the business of insurance in the State of Ohio.

lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Debt securities
lines.why: Bonds held for sale or to maturity: financial.

lines.name: Equity securities
lines.why: Shares held for their return: financial.

lines.name: Loans, net of the allowance
lines.why: Lending is a bank's business: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Deposits
lines.why: Customers' money a bank holds is its business: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Long-term debt (incl. current portion)
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans, current maturities included: financial.

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total liabilities minus the lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.
